question.prompt: Let \(\alpha\) be the radian measure of the smallest angle in a \(3\text{-}4\text{-}5\) right triangle. Let \(\beta\) be the radian measure of the smallest angle in a \(7\text{-}24\text{-}25\) right triangle. In terms of \(\alpha,\) what is \(\beta?\)

solutions.title: Match a double angle to a complement
solutions.explanation:
The side lengths suggest comparing \(\sin(2\alpha)\) with \(\cos\beta\). The smallest angle is opposite the shortest side, so
\[
\sin\alpha=\frac35,\qquad
\cos\alpha=\frac45,\qquad
\cos\beta=\frac{24}{25}.
\]
The sine double-angle formula now gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sin(2\alpha)
&=2\sin\alpha\cos\alpha\\
&=2\cdot\frac35\cdot\frac45\\
&=\frac{24}{25}
=\cos\beta
=\sin\left(\frac\pi2-\beta\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
Because \(\alpha\) is the smaller acute angle of a right triangle with unequal legs, \(0<\alpha<\pi/4\). Hence \(2\alpha\) is acute. Also, \(\pi/2-\beta\) is acute.

Sine is strictly increasing on the acute-angle interval, so the equal sine values imply
\[
2\alpha=\frac\pi2-\beta.
\]
Therefore \(\boxed{\beta=\frac\pi2-2\alpha}\), choice \(\text{C}\).

solutions.title: Compare cosine of twice the angle
